title: Critical Language Awareness
summary: How language constructs power and persuades: propaganda techniques, bias and omission, manipulative statistics, euphemism and doublespeak, inclusive and exclusive language, and register.

notes.text: Language is never neutral. Those with power, such as governments, companies and the media, choose words that shape how we see events. Critical readers ask: **Who wrote this? For whom? What is included, and what is left out? Who benefits?**

rows: A politician eating at a roadside stall
A sports star advertises a bank

notes.title: Naming a technique
notes.problem: 'Everyone is switching to Zapp. Don't be left behind.' Name the technique.
steps: It urges you to join what others are doing.
This is known as the bandwagon technique.

notes.text: **Doublespeak** deliberately hides the truth: 'rightsizing' or 'restructuring' for firing workers, 'collateral damage' for civilian deaths, 'price adjustment' for a price increase.

notes.title: Seeing through a euphemism
notes.problem: A company says it is 'rightsizing the workforce'. What does it mean, and why say it this way?
steps: Plain meaning: people are losing their jobs.
A pleasant phrase hides an unpleasant truth.
notes.answer: It is a euphemism for retrenching workers.

items: 'Up to 70% off': perhaps only one item.
Graphs with a vertical axis that does not start at zero exaggerate small differences.

notes.label: Inclusive and exclusive language
notes.text: Gender-neutral terms ('chairperson', 'firefighter', 'they') include everyone. 'Us and them' language ('those people') excludes and divides.

questions.prompt: Showing only the favourable facts about a product is called…
What is the term for language like 'rightsizing' that deliberately hides an unpleasant truth?
Which is the gender-neutral alternative to 'policeman'?
A graph whose vertical axis does not start at zero can exaggerate small differences.
Match each example to its propaganda technique.

pairs.left: 'My opponent is a puppet of big business.'
'If you don't vote for us, your jobs will vanish.'
A famous actor recommends a medicine

questions.prompt: A company announces a 'workforce optimisation programme'. Explain what this means and why the phrase is used.
questions.memo:
✓ It probably means retrenching/firing workers (1)
✓ The vague, positive phrase hides the harsh reality and protects the company's image (1)

questions.prompt: Why should readers question the headline 'Burglaries down 50% in Parkhurst!'?
questions.memo:
✓ We are not told the actual numbers; it could be a very small change (1)
✓ or a short, selective time period; statistics can be presented to mislead (1)

questions.prompt: Explain the effect of 'those people' in: 'Those people are taking our jobs.'
questions.memo:
✓ It creates an 'us and them' division (1)
✓ dehumanising and excluding a group, and encouraging prejudice (1)

questions.prompt: List THREE questions a critical reader should ask about a text.
questions.memo: Any three: ✓ Who wrote it? ✓ For whom/what audience? ✓ What is its purpose? ✓ What has been left out? ✓ Who benefits? (3)
